name: maybe_Ui_TenRowModePanes_Setup
signature: void maybe_Ui_TenRowModePanes_Setup(UiWindow* self, UiLayout* layout, u8 mode)
summary: Caches ten named row panes and one extra pane into a window: the ten names come from one of three 0x50-byte-separated name tables selected by the mode byte (2, 3 or other), and the extra pane from the matching table at +0x48. The three tables and the ten-iteration loop make the ten-row/mode name accurate.
evidence: The named callers are now Ui_ThreeModePaneWindow_InitPanes and Ui_ModeListWindow_InitPanes, which matches the two names in the old guess, and the body's fixed loop bound 10 plus the mode tests 2/3 confirm the layout. The body still contains unaff_r6 register spillage (damaged decompilation), so the name stays maybe_ at 0.35 rather than being promoted.

name: Ui_DiveWindow_ApplySelection
summary: Commits the current dive/event-window selection: resizes the bound container from the stored count, notifies the window through vtable +0x6C and selects the list entry at the current page.
evidence: The only caller is the named Ui_DiveWindow_HandleInputC, which is the class-specific input handler, so 'DiveWindow' is no longer a guess taken from a caller name; the body's named Container_SetCountFromByteSize and Ui_List_SelectEntryById calls complete the apply-selection sequence.

name: maybe_Ui_SetTwoSubPartsVisible
summary: Applies one visibility/state byte to two UI sub-parts at self+0x274 and self+0x29C by calling the pane-flag setter 0x0031893C twice with the same incoming argument.
evidence: The new context shows 0x0031893C is the split tail of the pane flag setter 0x00318920: it stores the byte at object+0x1C and rewrites bit 0 of the draw flag +0x44 on the two parts. Both calls in this 36-byte function pass the same incoming r1, so it is a two-part visibility setter, not a 'ProfileWindow copy sub-state'; the owner class is still only known as a UI object, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_UnregisterActorIfGateAllows
summary: Conditionally unregisters the actor slot embedded at self+0x3C: when the global gate byte and Field_CheckCameraOcclusionGate both allow it, it calls Ui_RegisterActor(self+0x3C, 0), which clears the slot.
evidence: The body contains no child-list detach at all; its only action is Ui_RegisterActor(self+0x3C, 0) behind Field_CheckCameraOcclusionGate(self+0x3C), so the old 'DetachChildListB' name described a function shape that is not present. The exact meaning of the camera gate and the owner is still unknown, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_RaisePendingEvent
signature: int maybe_Field_Object2D_RaisePendingEvent(GfxSpriteNode* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 ctx)
summary: If the object's pending byte f_2EC is set and the script event manager f_6C is idle, clears f_2EC and raises Script_Native_ATrgMapJumpEvent(eventMgr, f_2EE, f_2F0, 1); returns the manager status.
evidence: The named callee Script_Native_ATrgMapJumpEvent confirms the 'raise pending map-jump event once' reading and the old body has not changed; there is still no named caller (the function is reached through a vtable slot), so the owner class (2D sprite node vs field object) cannot be promoted.

name: maybe_Ui_CompareRow_SetOwnValueWithDifference
signature: void maybe_Ui_CompareRow_SetOwnValueWithDifference(void* self, int arg2, int diff)
summary: Expanded-mode compare row: writes the row's own recorded value (field +0xC via 0x00641090) into pane 2, the '/' separator into pane 3 and a '%d ls' difference into pane 4. This is the variant used when the compared item has an animation record, so the value is read from the row instead of the caller's category byte.
evidence: The caller Ui_CompareRow_SetValueFromChar calls this variant only when Ui_Part_FindAnimRecord succeeds, while the sibling 0x00475728 Ui_CompareRow_SetValueWithDifference takes the value from the caller; the body reads func_00641090(self,0xC) for pane 2. The old 'SetValueC' letter hid that distinction. The pane semantics are clear but the exact UI wording remains inferred, so it stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Battle_CheckStatusItemGate
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_CheckStatusItemGate(void* unit, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 ctx)
summary: Returns 1 only when the unit's vtable status queries for ids 0x5C..0x5F all report zero AND the party member mapped by unit[0x1DA] holds item 0x8B in one of the 24 inventory slots. Buff/debuff application calls it to decide whether to skip the normal apply path.
evidence: Disassembly of 0x001902CC (the previously unidentified callee) scans the 24 u16 inventory ids at member+0xEC for the requested id and returns the slot (or -1); with r2 == 0 it matches any slot. The object is therefore a party member, not a monster, and the function checks a status/item gate rather than proving status immunity. The vtable ids 0x5C..0x5F are still not identified, so the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Battle_CalcSkillEffectValue
signature: int maybe_Battle_CalcSkillEffectValue(void* skillRef, void* unit, int varianceMode)
summary: Computes a skill effect value from the skill record's min/max/threshold/curve fields: picks the unit stat selected by record+0xDF (unit+0x24 or +0x26), interpolates between record+0xC4/+0xC6 using the +0xC8 threshold and +0xCA cap, then adds a battle-RNG variance from record+0xCE (forced to -value for mode 1 or +value for mode 2).
evidence: func_0018C1B8 is the SkillRecord accessor per FACTS, and the body reads the record's +0xC4/+0xC6/+0xC8/+0xCA/+0xCE/+0xDF fields and calls the battle RNG 0x001CA474; there is no accuracy, dodge or hit test anywhere. The old 'CalcEvasionChance' name had no supporting operation. The field meanings are still inferred from the math, so maybe_ stays.

name: Battle_Monster_CalcBarScale
summary: Returns the monster HP-bar display scale as a float in s0: 1.0f when the unit's vtable +0x1C getter returns null, otherwise the dm->f_3CC table float scaled by 0.01 and adjusted through 0x00487FC0.
evidence: The Ghidra body is damaged (coprocessor_* instead of VFP), but the ARM listing is explicit: blx unit->vt[0x1C], vldreq s0,#1.0f on null, otherwise Game_GetDataManager -> 0x0063FD68 -> table float, multiply by 0.01f, compare and 0x00487FC0. The sole caller is the named Battle_Monster_CalcBarPercent, which multiplies its fraction by this value, so 'CalcBarScale' is proven by the disassembly.

name: maybe_Text_Row_InitFromRecord
summary: Only two operations survive in the readable body: fetch the game-data manager and call 0x0063D178 on its first word, after which the decompilation hits halt_baddata. The record id and every store are lost, so neither the row nor the record type can be pinned.
evidence: The caller is now Battle_PickWeightedCandidate and a tail symbol 0x0049AAFA exists, but the body is still truncated by bad instruction data; with no visible record id or stores the old 'Text_Row_InitFromRecord' label remains only a guess, kept below 0.50 as the decompilation is damaged.

name: Battle_Sequence_UpdateState
summary: Per-frame battle sequence state machine: advances the state word self[0x3B50] through the 0xF89/0xF8E/0xF93 branch set, waits on Ui_Window_IsGroupIdle, and drives Battle_Sequence_UpdateMemberAnchor and the actor/effect helpers.
evidence: The named callees Battle_Sequence_UpdateMemberAnchor and Ui_Window_IsGroupIdle, plus the state constants 0xF82..0xF93 and the battle-work fields 0x3B4D/0x3B50 already decoded, make the sequence-update reading specific; no other named function shares this state range.

name: Message_FormatArg5FromSpellRecord
summary: Resolves the SpellRecord for self->f_208, takes its +0x290 description message id, resolves that message text and formats it into message argument 5 using the literal format at 0x007BFD02; returns the caller's value unchanged.
evidence: 0x0063CFC8 is the SpellRecord accessor per FACTS, and the ARM call passes (5, 0x007BFD02, buffer) to 0x006D3EA0, i.e. sets message argument 5, not a log. The old 'Ui_InteractJob' owner had no support; the spell-record lookup and argument slot are explicit.

name: Message_FormatArg5FromSkillRecord
summary: Same formatter as 0x004A3C74 but for skills: resolves the SkillRecord for self->f_208, takes its +0xA0 description message id, resolves the text and formats it into message argument 5 using 0x007BFD0A; returns the caller's value.
evidence: 0x0063D018 is the SkillRecord accessor per FACTS and the ARM call again passes (5, format, buffer) to 0x006D3EA0. The record type and argument slot are now explicit; no 'interaction job' object is involved.

name: Actor_Action_IvyBase_Ctor
signature: void* Actor_Action_IvyBase_Ctor(void* mem, void* parent, void* actionDef, const char* name, int flags)
summary: Constructor of the base action object for the Ivy action family: runs Actor_ActionBase_Ctor and installs g_actorActionIvyBaseVtable, a vtable that adds no methods beyond the destructor and base thunks.
evidence: The sole caller is now the named Actor_CreateActionTable, the base call is Actor_ActionBase_Ctor, and the stored vtable is the named symbol g_actorActionIvyBaseVtable (not an anonymous address), so both the family and the construction role are established.

name: maybe_Field_ClearSceneEventFlags
summary: Clears three save-work story/event flags (ids 0x1A8, 0x1A7 and 0x1A9) by calling the save-work vtable +0x8 setter with value 0. It is invoked by Field_SceneNode_OnCommand for command 0, the node reset path.
evidence: The body never touches a model or animation instance: it takes Game_GetWork, gets the save-work object at +0x24A98 and calls its vtable+0x8 three times with constant ids 0x1A7/0x1A8/0x1A9 and value 0. The caller immediately sets another flag with value 1 in the same way, confirming the flag setter. The ids are still unidentified, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_Prop_SyncChildVisibility
summary: Validates the prop handle at +0x2CC, reads the config byte at config+0x1C and calls the child node's vtable+0x18 with 'config present and visible', so the prop's separate child visual follows the config state.
evidence: The named Field_HandleIsValid and Ui_ResolveObjectHandle calls frame the two sub-objects; the computed argument (f_2c8 != 0 && config->f_1C != 0) makes 'sync child visibility' more accurate than 'update', but the child type and config semantics are still unnamed fields, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Field_SceneNode_FlushPositions
summary: Walks the node's record list and copies each matching record's position (f_9C/f_A0/f_A4) into the per-object table returned by 0x00192F78(saveWork), matching on self->f_268 and the record's f_3AA/f_3AB index/status; then releases the two lists and the container at f_3C4.
evidence: The callees are GameWork/SaveData/Battle helpers, not list-window code, so the old 'Ui_ListWindow' prefix was wrong. The body writes three position words into a record indexed by f_318 and then performs the list/container teardown; the record table owner is still anonymous, so maybe_.

name: maybe_Field_CreateInteractableObject
summary: Small factory: allocates an object from the field pool through 0x0017C1C8 and stamps vtable 0x007781C4, nothing else. It is used while the map's NPC interactable-element resources are being set up.
evidence: The named callers Field_CreateActorData and the Field_LoadNpcIeResources path place it in NPC/IE setup, so 'IeObject' was too cryptic but the interactable-object role is supported. The 24-byte body proves only allocation + vtable stamping, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Field_BattleUnitObject_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a battle-unit-backed field object: installs the passed vtable, destroys the pack handle and the three 0xDC-byte sub-records, installs g_battleUnitObjectVtable on the base, releases the UI object and frees the block.
evidence: The callee set is now fully named (Pack_Handle_Dtor, std_destroy_range, 0x00200220 UI release, operator delete) and the base vtable is the named g_battleUnitObjectVtable, so the deleting-destructor role is solid; the previous 'Kind19' class number is not supported anywhere in the body, so the name is corrected but kept maybe_ because the concrete field-object class is unknown.

name: maybe_Field_Object_SetSpritePartVisible
summary: Command hook for a sprite-set part: mode 1 calls Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_SetPartVisible(partId, 1) and mode 2 calls it with 0; any other mode does nothing. The part id comes from self->f_4D and the sprite set from game work +0xB4; always returns 0.
evidence: The named callee Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_SetPartVisible proves this is a generic part-visibility toggle, not a 'talk' or mouth flag; nothing in the body refers to talking. The part id and owner remain unnamed, so maybe_ stays.

name: Field_Object_RegisterInRecordWindow
summary: Registers the object's two ids (f_46, f_48) in the shared record window through Ui_RecordWindow_InsertSorted on the menu manager at game work +0x7C, then returns 0.
evidence: Both callers are now the named Field_Scene_InitObjectTable and Field_Scene_UpdateObjectsFromTable, i.e. the scene object table, and the callee is the named Ui_RecordWindow_InsertSorted; the two ids are inserted in sorted order as the name says.

name: maybe_Ui_UmaWindow_DeletingDtor2
summary: Deleting-destructor wrapper for the second horse-race (Uma) window vtable: runs Ui_UmaWindow_Dtor_2 and frees the object with operator delete.
evidence: It is vtable 0x0077A104 slot 0 beside the named Ui_UmaWindow_InitTextPanels/Ui_UmaWindow_Update, and it calls Ui_UmaWindow_Dtor_2 then 0x0010F6CC. A confirmed Ui_UmaWindow_DeleteDtor already exists at 0x004CCF34 for vtable 0x0077874C, so this second vtable needs the '2' suffix to stay unique.

name: Ui3D_AttachRecordEntries
summary: Walks the element's entry-record block (unless the current scene mode is masked out), resolves each entry's actor object and animation, re-initialises its draw parameters and re-attaches it to the render list through Ui_ActorSlot_BindActor.
evidence: The sibling 0x004E55AC Ui3D_UpdateAttackSequence now proves this is the Ui3DElement class (same vtable family), and the callers Field_Scene_InitObjectTable/UpdateObjectsFromTable supply the entry table; the named Ui_ActorSlot_BindActor and animation lookups complete the attach path.

name: Ui3D_TryStartAttackSequence
summary: Starts the element's attack animation: refuses while the scene mode is 2 with the pause byte clear, otherwise runs the 0x46E7F4 gate and, on success, seeds the two countdowns at self+0x48/0x4C with 0.21 s and 0.48 s and clears the state byte self+0x45.
evidence: The sibling Ui3D_UpdateAttackSequence (0x004E55AC) documents f_45 as the attack state and says f_48/f_4C are the two countdowns seeded with 0.21/0.48 by this function; the constants 0x3E570A3D and 0x3EF5C290 match those values exactly.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_DeletingDtorA
summary: Deleting destructor of the first message-window variant: installs vtable 0x0077B214 and its secondary table at +0x258, releases the embedded handle at +0x2F4 through Field_HandleRelease/Pack_Handle_Dtor, runs the 2D effect-node destructor and frees the block.
evidence: The sequence *self = vtable; secondary = vtable+0xD4; Field_HandleRelease; Pack_Handle_Dtor; 0x0028EFB4; operator delete is a deleting destructor, not a constructor; the old 'DtorBody' wording hid the delete. The concrete window class behind vtable 0x0077B214 is still unproven, so maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_DeletingDtorB
summary: Deleting destructor of the second message-window variant: installs vtable 0x0077B30C and its secondary table, releases the embedded handle at +0x2FC, runs the effect-node destructor and frees the block.
evidence: Same destructor chain as 0x004E650C but with vtable 0x0077B30C and the member at +0x2FC; the deleting-destructor shape is explicit. The class behind this vtable is still unproven, so maybe_ and the B suffix remain.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_QueueStatePopup
summary: Checks the first child's status ids 6 and 7 and queues one 16-byte message entry through Battle_MessageQueue_PushEntry: code 0x13 when id 6 is set, code 0xFD when id 7 is set instead.
evidence: The named Battle_MessageQueue_PushEntry call and the caller Battle_ActionSequence_WaitUnitState fix the battle-message posting role, but the exact meaning of popup codes 0x13/0xFD and the TextWindow owner are not decoded, so maybe_ stays.

name: Field_Object_Kind09_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the field object produced by script object factory kind 9: runs FieldParty_Ctor, installs vtable 0x0077C9F8, seeds the three words at 0x3784..0x3786 with -1/0/-1024.0f and clears f_3787 and the byte at +0xDE1D.
evidence: The sole caller is the named Field_ObjectFactory_Kind09 and the base call is the named FieldParty_Ctor, so both the kind and the constructor role are established by names rather than by the address alone.

name: maybe_Ui_ListWindow_FillStatRows
signature: void maybe_Ui_ListWindow_FillStatRows(UiListWidget* self, const void* stats, int arg3, void* callback)
summary: Generic list filler: walks the eleven-entry getter table at 0x0072CCB0 (icon byte, getter, extra flag), formats each positive value into a pane row and blanks the remaining columns through the shared string/pane helpers.
evidence: The table and the Ui_ListWindow_HideUnusedRows helper are unchanged; the function is still reached only through the 0x77D9EC filler dispatch table. The table's getters look like stat readers, but no caller names the screen, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_ListWindow_FillExtraRows
signature: void maybe_Ui_ListWindow_FillExtraRows(UiListWidget* self, const void* source, unsigned int arg3, void* callback)
summary: Second list filler: same getter table as 0x004FB1CC but writes six panes per row (text id 0xAA plus the formatted number and separators) and appends a generic icon in the last column.
evidence: The skeleton, 0x0072CCB0 table and dispatch entry (0x77F4A8) are the same as the stat filler, but there is no named caller and no string that identifies the owning list, so the 'ExtraRows' wording stays a guess and the name remains maybe_.

name: Ui_SceneWindow_Close
summary: Closes the party scene window: resets the member models, releases the scene resource slot and notifies the UI overlay manager at game work +0x48.
evidence: The named callees FieldParty_ResetMemberModels and Ui_Overlay_SetMarkerState, plus the actor-action release, form the complete party-scene teardown; the old maybe_ was only waiting for those callee names.

name: maybe_Gfx_StreamSlot_AllocEntry
summary: Allocates an 8-byte VRAM bookkeeping entry into the slot's first word and, on success, clears the slot counters f_58/f_5C and the busy byte +6. Returns whether the allocation succeeded.
evidence: The callee Gfx_Vram_AllocEntry(void** out) writes the new entry through its out pointer; here r0 is the slot itself, so the entry is stored at self[0], which the old 'ReleaseIfDone' reading missed. The caller Gfx_StreamSlot_Init uses it as the per-slot allocator and Gfx_Movie_AdvanceTimeline reuses it for the ring, so 'AllocEntry' is the honest role although the exact ring semantics remain inferred.

name: maybe_Gfx_ReleaseDeviceObject
summary: Releases one device/resource handle through the global callback dispatcher 0x006B8FB8 and clears the caller's pointer.
evidence: Both callers are the named Gfx_StreamSlot_Release and Gfx_StreamSlot_Shutdown, which confirms a teardown helper; the callee is still only known as maybe_Gfx_RenderCallback_Dispatch, so what exactly the handle points at remains unproven and maybe_ stays.

name: Gfx_MovieSurface_Ctor
signature: u32 Gfx_MovieSurface_Ctor(GfxMovieSurfaces* self, u32 w, u32 h, u32 decoder, u32 b, u32* c)
summary: Constructor of the decoded-frame surface set: allocates the 3 x 2 plane groups with Gfx_MovieSurface_Allocate, converts the size words to floats for the decoder and wires the per-channel release helpers.
evidence: The sole caller is now the named Gfx_Movie_StartPlayback_2, and the callees are the named Gfx_MovieSurface_Allocate, Gfx_StreamSlot_Destroy and Gfx_MovieSurface_SetupDescriptor; the 3 x 2 allocation loops match the surface layout.

name: Fs_WorkBuffer_Init
summary: Zeroes an 0xE30-byte file-service request/work buffer and stamps its first word with type 5.
evidence: All three callers are now named file-service paths (Fs_BuildRequestArgs, Svc_Content_ResolveEntryType, and the debug-label init that reuses the same buffer) and the size/type constants are explicit; nothing in the body is sound-specific, so 'Fs_WorkBuffer_Init' replaces the old Sound_ guess.

name: maybe_Svc_Content_TranslateResultList
summary: Translates an array of 8-byte service result entries into engine status codes by switching on each entry's kind byte (+4): 0 -> 0x8C, 1 -> 0x0D, 3 -> 0x10, 4 -> 0x30, and builds the per-entry payload word.
evidence: The caller is Fs_BuildRequestArgs and the callees are Svc_Ipc_Cmd1007Thunk/Fs_FillRequestBlock, which match the file-service result path; the body still carries damaged register/flag values (unaff_r8/in_NG) so the per-entry mapping cannot be fully verified and maybe_ stays.

name: Snd_RequestArchiveEntry
signature: int Snd_RequestArchiveEntry(ContentEntry* entry, int arg2, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Formats a 16-hex-digit id from an entry record (kind 0/1/3/4 -> 0x8C/0x0D/0x10/0x30 plus the packed id/type word) and sends it as the string of the snd:u command-3 request.
evidence: The named callee Svc_Snd_Cmd0003SendString uses the proven 0x007AEAB0 snd:u session, and the '%016llx' format plus the entry fields are explicit; the caller Fs_ValidateRequestEntry hands it a request entry, so the sound-archive request role is established.

name: maybe_Svc_Object_Cmd8
signature: void maybe_Svc_Object_Cmd8(SvcObject* object, u32 request, u32 second, u32 third, u32 request2, u32 fifth, u32 flag)
summary: Slot 1 of the service-object vtable: obtains the checked object handle and forwards six arguments plus the packed flag word to Svc_Ipc_Send08030102 (command header 0x08030102).
evidence: The named callees Svc_Object_GetHandleChecked and Svc_Ipc_Send08030102 confirm it is a command forwarder, but the meaning of command 0x08030102 is still unknown, so the positional 'Cmd8' name is kept with maybe_.

name: maybe_Fs_ArchiveEntry_SeekByMode
signature: int maybe_Fs_ArchiveEntry_SeekByMode(FsEntry* self, uint32_t where, uint32_t offsetLo, int offsetHi, int mode)
summary: Implements all three archive-entry seek modes: 0 = absolute, 1 = relative to the current position, 2 = relative to the end; it computes the 64-bit position and delegates to Fs_ArchiveEntry_SetReadPosition, returning 0xE0E046BD for an unknown mode.
evidence: The mode chain is fully readable and handles absolute/relative/end, so 'SeekRelative' described only one third of it; the named callers Fs_ArchiveEntry_Seek/Fs_ArchiveStream_SeekTo confirm the seek role. The body still uses unaff_r4/unaff_r5 (damaged decompilation), so confidence stays just below 0.50.

name: maybe_Ui_IconCache_CopyTimestamp
summary: Writes one 8-byte icon-index field into the caller's buffer: a non-null source is copied by 0x0011FFFC, a null source takes the initialiser 0x006722EC; returns the out pointer.
evidence: The caller Ui_IconCache_WriteIndexTable uses it for the 'ERROR   ' literal when an entry is missing and for the entry name otherwise, so it is an 8-byte record-field writer rather than a timestamp converter. The exact source type is still unnamed, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_IconCache_IsPresent
summary: Probes the cache service through self->vtable+0x2C with two flags, returning the service's status and using maybe_Svc_ContentObject_QuerySize to latch whether the requested content is present.
evidence: The caller Ui_IconCache_CommitEntry and the named maybe_Svc_ContentObject_QuerySize callee support the cache-presence reading, but the function returns a service status word (not a clean bool) and the two vtable queries are unidentified, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Svc_Blob_Serialize
summary: Serialises a blob into a caller buffer: copies the 0x70-byte header, writes each of blob->f_130 entries as an 8-byte sub-header plus 4-byte-padded payload, then the main payload and the 0x20-byte trailer; returns the blob's size word.
evidence: The named caller Ui_IconCache_WorkerThread and the clear copy/pad sequence support the serializer reading, but the other callers are still unnamed/misnamed and the blob type is not proven, so maybe_ stays.

name: Regex_Buffer_Init
signature: u32 Regex_Buffer_Init(TextBuffer* self, u32 size, u32 count, int clear)
summary: Allocates and initialises the regex scratch buffer: (count+0xF)>>4 units through 0x00514390, optionally clears the first count bytes, and stores capacity/size at +0x18/+0x1C and +0x08/+0x14.
evidence: Both callers are named regex functions (Regex_State_FindOrCreate, Regex_Match_Build) and the allocation/field initialisation matches the buffer the regex states consume; the old Text_ prefix came only from the generic allocation shape.

name: maybe_Regex_OpReplaceOutputList
signature: u32 maybe_Regex_OpReplaceOutputList(RegexCursor* cursor, RegexValueList** out, RegexCursor** left, RegexCursor* right)
summary: Regex opcode that rewrites the destination value list: with the zero flag it clears the old node list and pushes one value from the right operand; otherwise it iterates the operands, builds their successor lists and appends the values.
evidence: The callees Container_Variant_ClearChildren/AddChild and maybe_Regex_BuildSuccessorList fit an opcode handler, but there is no caller (it is an opcode-table entry) and the left/right cursor roles are inferred, so the exact 'replace' wording remains unproven and maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Regex_BuildSuccessorList
signature: u32 maybe_Regex_BuildSuccessorList(RegexValue* node, RegexValueList** out, RegexList* operands, RegexList* visited)
summary: Builds the value set for one regex expression node: allocates a memo entry, hangs it off the node, records the operand/visited links and recursively copies the operand values into the result list.
evidence: The named callers Regex_OpBuildOperandSets/Regex_OpBuildOperandSetsSingle show it is called per operand node and its result is a value set, so 'successor list' is only a working label; the memo/visited layout is still inferred, so maybe_ at 0.40.

name: Os_SvcCommand90040
summary: Issues the one-parameter SVC request 0x00090040 with a shared-resource id through software interrupt 0x32 and returns the kernel's result word.
evidence: The body explicitly stores command 0x00090040 and the resource id in the thread block, executes svc 0x32 and returns the result; the named callers Svc_ObjectPool_InitA/InitB call it to acquire the shared resource, so the mechanical SVC-wrapper name is accurate.

name: Gfx_EnsureGpuSession
summary: Opens the gsp::Gpu session on first use: takes the GPU lock, opens the handle into 0x007AF18C, mirrors it into the block's f_14 and submits the open IPC; when already open it only re-sends the IPC.
evidence: The session block is 0x007AF178 whose name pointer is the rodata string at 0x0078C495 = 'gsp::Gpu'; the callers are now named graphics/font/model paths (Gfx_ModelResource_Release, Gfx_ModelInstance_InitFromResource, Gfx_Flim_Parse, Font_BuildDisplayList), so 'EnsureGpuSession' is proven.

name: maybe_Sound_GetDriverParam
signature: int maybe_Sound_GetDriverParam(unsigned arg1, unsigned arg2, unsigned arg3, unsigned arg4)
summary: Reads one byte parameter under the scheduler lock: locks, issues Gfx_IpcCmd90040(arg1, &out), aborts on a hard error, unlocks and returns the resulting byte.
evidence: The caller is the named Sound_Driver_Init, which supports the sound-driver-parameter reading, but the only callee is the low-level command wrapper 0x0011A36C and the argument's meaning is unknown; the old maybe_ is kept.

name: maybe_Mem_PoolSlot_Allocate
signature: void* maybe_Mem_PoolSlot_Allocate(PoolOwner* owner, ObjectSlotDesc* desc, uint32_t kind, uint32_t index, uint32_t sub, uint32_t arg6)
summary: Allocates a 0x5880-byte slot from the fixed object pool, links it into the owner's slot list and fills the slot header (kind, owner, descriptor id, zeroed counters); returns null when the pool is exhausted.
evidence: The callers Gfx_ModelInstance_Init/InitWithTransform and the fixed 0x5880 stride support the pool-slot reading, but the body is damaged (SBORROW4/unaff values around the pool index), so the exact field semantics cannot be verified and maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Gfx_ModelPart_ReleaseAll
summary: Releases every 0x3C-byte part record of a part list (count from self->f_C+8, records at self->f_18): frees each part's GPU blocks through Mem_FreeGraphicsBlock, optionally keeping the caller's part, and drops the tracked resources.
evidence: The callers are now Gfx_ModelSlot_Replace and Fx_SpawnEmitter, i.e. model-slot replacement/emitter setup, and the named Mem_FreeGraphicsBlock/Gfx_UnregisterResources calls confirm the release pass; the body still has unaff_r4 and the list owner is not fully proven, so maybe_ stays.
